newsitem.title: PERU: Peru police fear PLO moves on Jewish, U.S. targets.
newsitem.headline: Peru police fear PLO moves on Jewish, U.S. targets.

text.p: Peru's anti-terrorist police say Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) members have arrived in Peru to attack Jewish and U.S. targets this month, according to a document Reuters obtained on Tuesday.

PLO members who entered the country on March 31 "plan to carry out a series of terrorist acts against Jewish installations in Peru -- likewise against U.S. interests," the three-paragraph police report written on May 3 said.

The group plans to strike on important anniversaries in the Jewish calendar, including this week's celebration of the creation of the state of Israel, the internal report said, without ruling out attacks during the first week of June.
The document instructs anti-terrorist police to "detect, locate, capture and/or neutralise the terrorists of the fundamentalist organisation."

The PLO is not known to have carried out attacks in Peru, but the United States blames Middle Eastern groups for the bombings in Argentina of the Israeli Embassy in 1992 and a Jewish community centre in 1994, in which more than 100 people died.

Peru's security forces are also on alert for reprisal attacks by the country's Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) after the military killed 14 of its rebels in a hostage rescue strike last month at the Japanese ambassador's home.

In its propaganda, Peru's larger and more violent guerrilla group, Shining Path, is warning it intends to create a "Bloody May" that could add to the 30,000 lives lost in the country's 17 years of guerrilla conflicts, police sources say.
